problem: The symbol m is reused with two different meanings. Section 1 defines m as the number of feature functions, but here 'Z(x) sums over mⁿ sequences' and 'O(n m²)' need m to be the number of labels. A student will read 'mⁿ' as (feature functions)ⁿ, which is wrong, and will not see where the label-set size comes from in the O(n m²) cost. Section 1 already introduced |Y(x)| = 2ⁿ for that count.
fix: Write: Z(x) sums over |Y|ⁿ label sequences, where |Y| is the number of labels — too many to list. The forward algorithm computes it in O(n |Y|²) by passing a vector of partial sums along the chain. Viterbi uses the same chain but replaces sum with max, returning argmax_y P(y | x) in O(n |Y|²). Keep m for the number of feature functions only.
